newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan prosecutors indict Hamanaka - media reports.
newsitem.headline: Japan prosecutors indict Hamanaka - media reports.

text.p: Japanese prosecutors on Monday indicted Sumitomo Corp's former star copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka on a charge of fraud, local media reported.
The move follows Sumitomo's announcement last month that it had filed a complaint against Hamanaka with prosecutors alleging fraud, Kyodo news agency said.

Hamanaka was arrested on October 22 on suspicion that he forged two documents in 1994 in connection with Sumitomo's estimated $2.6 billion loss from copper trades. He was served the second arrest warrant for alleged fraud while in detention.
He was seen as the most influential player in the world copper market until he was fired by Sumitomo on June 14.
Officials at the prosecutors' office could not immediately be reached for comment.
